name: Биом 3 «Библиотека Улариона», враги заново — 14 портретов по способу «Глубокий промт персонажа» (art/style/style.md). Замечание автора 29.09.2026 о прежней партии (jobs/biome-03-library.json): дворфы — «каменное создание, которое еле ходит», не серьёзные враги; нужны пафос, прописанная поза, детали личности, характер в портрете. Арена биома 3 принята, здесь её нет. Что изменено против прежнего задания: 1) каждый промт — слои «кто он и чего хочет сейчас · характер в лице, взгляде и осанке · поза словами: вес, плечи, голова, взгляд, обе руки, оружие, миг действия · пять личных деталей · место»; 2) куклы Библиотеки — шедевры Мастерской: пропорции воина-дворфа, скульптурная резьба, ухоженная бронза, у каждого своё лицо; «глаза не понимают написанного» теперь не пустые глаза, а живой янтарный взгляд, в котором нет понимания письма, — есть цель; 3) кадр теснее и ниже: пояс по нижнему краю, камера чуть снизу — фигура возвышается; прежде половина кукол вышла в рост; 4) у каждого своё место в Библиотеке, а не одинаковые стеллажи с часами; 5) Смотритель — башенные часы-собор на коленчатых ногах, а не котёл на ножках. Облик и лор — docs/content/враги-биомов.md, раздел 3; способности — design/ui/biome-foes.js (b3o1…b3g1): портрет говорит то же, что способности. Правила ADR-0012 и ADR-0013: без картинки в запросе, враг в действии, корпус развёрнут влево. Руны на плитах и цилиндрах — только фактура тонких линий: текст в арте — брак. Звери и аппарат кадрируются по своему описанию, чтобы не было противоречия «ног не видно» и «передние лапы» (в прежней партии оно дало цикл самоисправления)
style: Art style: hand-painted stylized dark-fantasy game art for a mobile RPG. Painterly digital illustration with visible, confident brush strokes and simplified planar shapes, crisp rim light on edges, strong readable silhouettes, deep near-black shadows. Epic, dramatic character art: a powerful pose, a low camera, strong theatrical light from below. Light tells the story: a few strong sources — the sand of hourglasses, cracks in the stone floor and fine grooves in old stone that glow from within — throw warm amber light upward, the light comes from below. Warm and cold light contrast. Dust motes and fine stone grit float in the light. Moderate detail, clean readable forms; the face, the hands and the weapon get the most detail. No photorealism, no 3D-render look, no anime, no cartoon.
negative: No text, no letters, no numbers, no glyphs, no runes that look like letters, no real-world scripts, no carvings that look like writing or numerals, no occult symbols, no watermark, no signature, no logo, no UI elements, no border or frame around the picture. Tablets, cylinders, cords and walls carry no writing and no signs: only fine worn grooves and texture. No gore, no blood, no skulls, no horror grotesque. No purple, no violet, no magenta light. Only one figure in the foreground; a figure shaped like a dwarf has exactly two arms and two hands. Not a mannequin, not a crash-test dummy, not a marionette on strings, not a clumsy golem, not a robot, not a statue on display: no stiff, passive, awkward or doll-like pose, no dead or empty eyes.

enemies.frame: Draw exactly one image in a single pass: no alternative versions, no second attempts, no text in the reply. Enemy card portrait, 4:5. The card is shown small on the battle field (about 74 px wide) and large in the bestiary, so the enemy must read as one bold, simple, well-lit silhouette with a clear pose against a darker background. Framing: a close, heroic half-length portrait. The camera is a little below the figure's chest and looks slightly up, so the enemy towers over the viewer and fills most of the frame. A figure shaped like a dwarf is cut by the bottom edge of the picture at the belt: head, shoulders, chest, arms and hands in the frame, no hips, no legs, no feet. Beasts and machines are framed as their own description says. The head sits in the upper third with a little space above it. The body is turned in three-quarter view toward the LEFT side of the picture, where its enemies stand; its weapon, its spell or the thing it is named after is thrust toward the left, in front of the body, and reads clearly. Pathos: it is a worthy and dangerous enemy — powerful, proud, alive and caught at the peak of an action, a foe that is frightening and honourable to defeat. Its character shows in its face, its gaze and its posture; its story shows in the details of its body and its tools. No one in this set wears a hood. World: the Library of Ularion, the workshop of the god of knowledge deep under the city of Endalor — a real ancient library cut in dark stone. Its halls go down and down; on long stone shelves lie stone tablets and stone cylinders covered with long, straight, parallel engraved grooves, like ruled lines with nothing written between them — the writing that only the god can read shows only as this worn texture of straight lines, never as letters, squiggles or signs. On the worktables parts of dwarves and parts of mechanisms lie together: the god made the people and the machine with the same hands. At every work place stands an hourglass of bronze and glass with glowing amber sand. Stone beetles live in the shelves; stone sagans are rock that has noticed itself. The Library's servants are stone dwarves made by the god. The Library calls them puppets, but they are masterworks, made carefully and with pride: carved from dark grey stone with the precision of great sculpture, polished smooth where they move and left with fine chisel marks elsewhere; the proportions of dwarf warriors — very broad shoulders, a deep chest, a thick neck, massive forearms, big capable hands; strong individual faces with heavy brows and broad noses, carved beards bound with bronze rings; bronze ball joints — precise, well-oiled work with thin engraved bands of straight lines — at the neck, shoulders, elbows and wrists, unless the description says otherwise. Their eyes are inlaid stones that glow from within, amber unless the description says otherwise: alive, attentive, fixed on the enemy with purpose. Their hands know the work and the fight; only the writing they cannot understand. They move with weight and certainty, like veteran warriors and master craftsmen. Colors: muted, like all our enemies — dark grey basalt, warm dull bronze and old brass, soot black, dusty ochre; everything else sinks into near-black shadow. Light, the same for the whole set: the light comes from below — warm amber light from the sand of the hourglasses, from cracks in the stone floor and from the grooves of the tablets rises onto the figure and lights its face and hands from underneath; crisp cool grey-blue rim light on its edges is the only cold light. Background: its own place in the Library, darker and softer than the figure, with depth. All fourteen portraits of this set share the same framing, painting style, palette and lighting.

jobs.subject_v1: The enemy: the Unbending, a rank-and-file brawler of the Library (Earth). Who he is: a stone dwarf warrior whom the god carved without joints at the elbows — each arm is a single piece of dark stone from the bronze ball of the shoulder to the heavy square fist. He was made to hold the line and never bend, and right now he wants one thing: to break through the heroes on the left. Character: unyielding, stubborn, proud that he has never bowed. It shows in his face: a heavy brow lowered, a jaw clenched like a vice, nostrils flared, amber eyes burning steadily at his foe; his neck and back are straight as a pillar. Pose, the moment of the blow: he cannot bend, so he strikes with his whole body. His weight is thrown forward toward the left and his torso is twisted hard from the waist in a huge horizontal sweep: the near arm, straight and rigid like a stone club, swings across the front of his body toward the left, fist first, and has just smashed into stone — a wide fan of sharp stone shards bursts toward the left from the point of impact (Earth); the far arm, just as straight, is flung back behind him by the force of the swing. His chin is tucked and his head lowered behind his leading shoulder like a ram's, eyes fixed on the target. Details that tell his story: (1) where the elbows should be, the stone runs on unbroken, and a plain bronze band is sealed around it — he was made this way on purpose; (2) his square fists are chipped and worn smooth by a thousand blows; (3) his beard is carved straight and stiff like a spade, without braids, bound by one heavy bronze ring; (4) a heavy bronze collar sits on his shoulders like a yoke; (5) a web of old cracks across his chest has been filled with bronze by the Library's fitters. Place: a long straight aisle between tall stone shelves; behind him a thick stone pillar bears a fist-shaped crater with cracks running out of it; amber light glows from the cracks of the floor below.

jobs.subject: The enemy: the Loose One, a rank-and-file skirmisher of the Library (Earth). Who he is: a lean, wiry stone dwarf whose bronze joints have worked loose over the centuries — and he has found a use for it: one of his arms unfolds like a carpenter's folding ruler and reaches farther than any blade. Right now he is reaching past the heroes' front line for the one who is already wounded. Character: sly, twitchy and predatory — a scavenger who always picks the weakest. His head hangs tilted on a loose neck joint at a hungry angle, one amber eye narrowed and the other wide open, the corner of his carved mouth pulled up in a crooked, knowing grin. Pose, the moment of the reach: he leans his upper body far forward toward the left, low, the shoulder of his reaching arm pushed ahead. That arm shoots out toward the left and unfolds in a zigzag of six straight stone segments joined by small bronze hinges, stretching almost to the left edge of the picture; at its end a stone hand with long sharpened stone fingers is spread like a claw, about to seize. His other arm hangs loose at his side, the hand dangling from a slack wrist joint. He has exactly two arms, both attached at the shoulders. Details that tell his story: (1) his loose joints rattle, and little puffs of stone dust shake out of them as he moves; (2) one hinge pin is missing and has been replaced with a bent bronze nail; (3) each segment of the folding arm has small evenly spaced notches along its edge, like a measuring rule, without any numbers; (4) his fingertips are filed to points; (5) his short beard is ragged and chipped at the ends. Place: a high gallery of the Library at the edge of a dark drop, stone tablets knocked off a shelf by his arm and falling; amber light glowing from the cracks of the floor below.

jobs.subject: The enemy: the Whispering Rubble, a rank-and-file mage of the Library (Earth). Who it is: a stone sagan — a swarm of grey grit and sharp chips of broken tablets that has noticed itself and learned that it can be someone. It gathers into the shape of a tall figure: head, shoulders, chest and two arms of hovering, swirling stones; below the chest it dissolves into a whirling column of grit — it has no legs. Right now it wants to bury everyone who came into its hall. Character: newborn, hungry and exultant — the terrible joy of a thing that has just discovered it can destroy. Its face is formed out of hundreds of small stones: a sharp brow, deep hollows for eyes with amber light burning far inside, and an open mouth from which ribbons of fine grit pour out and are sucked back in — it whispers without pause. Pose, the peak of the spell: it rises to its full height and flings both arms up and wide toward the left; above the left side of the picture a storm of stones gathers in the air and begins to fall in a heavy rockfall onto its enemies (Earth). Its head is thrown slightly back, its chest open, stones streaming from its shoulders into the storm. Details that tell its story: (1) among the grit spin fragments of broken stone tablets with fine grooves on them — it is made of the Library's broken writings, and it whispers them; (2) warm amber light pulses in the gaps between its stones like a heartbeat; (3) its edges keep crumbling and gathering again, fine dust trailing off in spirals; (4) a few larger chips circle its head like a crown. Place: a hall where a whole stone shelf has collapsed, a heap of broken tablets below it; dust hangs in the amber light rising from the cracks of the floor.

jobs.subject_v1: The enemy: the Stone Beetle, a rank-and-file tank of the Library (Earth). Who it is: a beetle of living stone as big as a travelling chest; it lives in the lowest shelves and has defended its shelf for centuries. Right now it charges to throw the intruders back from the tablets. Character: territorial, stubborn and unstoppable — a small fortress that has never given ground. Its two faceted eyes glint amber, alert and angry. Framing and pose, the moment of the charge: it is a beast. The camera is low, at the height of the floor, and looks slightly up at it; its head, its heavy front shell and its two front legs fill the frame, and the rest of its body goes back out of the frame; its head points toward the left. It rushes toward the left with its head low and the thick, blunt front edge of its shell raised like a ram and a shield at once; its short, powerful mandibles are open; its front legs are driven hard into the floor, and the slabs crack and burst under them in a spray of stone chips and dust flying to the left (Earth). Details that tell its story: (1) its grey stone shell is covered with fine criss-cross scratches from squeezing between the shelves for centuries — scratches only, no signs; (2) warm amber light glows from the seams between its shell plates; (3) one front corner of its shell was broken off long ago, and the break has healed with a seam of glowing amber; (4) the front edge of its shell is polished to a shine by ramming; (5) stone dust and a small chip of a tablet are caught in the joints of its legs. Place: the bottom shelf of a huge stone bookcase — its home — with tablets knocked over around it; amber light glowing in the cracks of the floor below.

jobs.subject: The enemy: the Leaking One, a rank-and-file healer of the Library (Earth). Who he is: an old stone dwarf whose bronze joints all leak oil, all the time. He oils the joints of his kin until his own oil runs out — and while he stands, they do not fall. Right now he is giving his oil to a wounded brother behind him. Character: devoted and sorrowful, but unshakable — a quiet martyr who has decided to give everything. His carved face is lined and kind, his brows drawn together in grief, but his amber eyes are fixed on the heroes, defiant: you will not take them while I have a drop. Pose, the moment of the gift: he stands squarely, his shoulders set toward the left and his chin raised. His near hand is raised toward the left, palm open — a stern warning to the heroes to come no further; his far hand lifts a cupped palm brimming with glowing amber oil up and back over his shoulder, and the oil pours in a shining stream onto a wounded kin behind him, beyond the edge of the picture. Details that tell his story: (1) glowing amber oil runs from every bronze joint — neck, shoulders, elbows, wrists — and over the centuries it has streaked his stone body dark; (2) in the middle of his chest sits a small bronze reservoir with a round glass window, almost empty — only a little glowing oil is left at its bottom; (3) his long carved beard in two braids is soaked and darkened with oil at the tips; (4) his fingertips are stained dark from oiling others; (5) old rags are wound around his own joints, never tightened. Place: a narrow repair niche of the Library with pegs of spare bronze joints on the wall and an hourglass whose amber sand has almost run out; oil stains on the stone floor, amber light from the cracks below.

jobs.subject_v1: The enemy: the Erased, a rare and deadly assassin of the Library (Air). Who she is: a stone dwarf woman — short, compact and wiry, beardless — from whom every mark was scraped off long ago, and her name and her work were erased with them. Now it is as if she does not exist. She walks without a sound between the shelves and comes out right at the one who heals. Right now she has chosen the heroes' healer. Character: cold, silent, patient and merciless — absence used as a weapon. Her face is fine and calm, with high cheekbones and a closed mouth; her eyes are two narrow slits of pale cold light, fixed on her target without blinking. Pose, the moment of the strike: she has just slipped out of a narrow gap between two shelves and lunges low and fast toward the left, leaning far forward, her shoulders leading; her near hand holds a long, thin bronze erasing knife — the kind used to scrape writing off tablets — in a reversed grip, the blade along her forearm, about to strike; her far hand trails behind her for balance, fingers spread. A thin cold draught (Air) follows her and pulls a trail of dust out of the gap behind her. Details that tell her story: (1) her whole pale grey stone body is covered with long parallel scrape marks — even her cheek and brow — everything was scraped smooth, not one sign is left; (2) her bronze joints are tightly wrapped in dark cloth so they make no sound; (3) the erasing knife is worn thin and curved like a crescent from centuries of scraping; (4) her hair is carved close to her head in smooth, simple bands, scraped smooth like the rest; (5) she is half in shadow — the light finds only her face, the knife and the edge of her shoulder. Place: the dark gap between two tall stone shelves; on the nearest shelf lies a stone tablet scraped completely blank; faint amber light rises from the floor below, and a cold grey-blue light runs along her edges.

jobs.subject: The enemy: the Fitter, an elite brawler of the Library (Earth). Who he is: the master fitter of the Library's worktables, a heavy, powerful stone dwarf with a bronze hammer and a box of joints. For a thousand years he has knocked parts into place — and knocked them out. He sees every body as a set of parts. Right now he has found a part that does not fit: the hero in front of him. Character: confident, brutal and practical, with a craftsman's pride — he is not angry, he is working. His brows are lowered in concentration, his amber eyes measure the target coldly, his mouth is set in a grim, satisfied line. Pose, the moment of the blow: he has raised a heavy bronze hammer high over his head with both hands, his torso arched back and twisted, his shoulders rolled back — all his weight about to come down in a single blow toward the left. The hammer head is large and close to the camera near the top of the picture. Bronze pins and hinges jump out of the box at his side from the force of the swing, stone chips fly. Details that tell his story: (1) the hammer has a long handle wound with worn leather, its bronze face dented by a thousand blows; (2) a wide leather strap across his chest holds a battered wooden box of spare bronze joints at his hip; (3) his own body is fitted from mismatched parts — one forearm is of a lighter stone than the rest, joined at the elbow with a newer bronze ring: he fitted himself; (4) bronze calipers hang from his belt; (5) his long braided beard is tucked into his belt so it does not catch in the work. jobs.subject: The enemy: the Knot-Tier, an elite debuffer of the Library (Earth). Who he is: the Library's keeper of accounts. A cord is wound around his belt, and hundreds of knotted cords hang from it: each knot is a record — whose strength, and how much. When he ties a knot on you, your strength goes into the cord; when he ties a deaf knot, your healer falls silent. Right now he is counting the heroes. Character: cold, calculating and quick — a bookkeeper of other people's strength. His head is tilted slightly, his amber eyes narrowed as if adding up sums, a thin, satisfied smile under a long braided beard. Pose, the moment of the knot: he holds a long cord stretched taut between his two hands toward the left, as if measuring the hero in front of him, and with a sharp jerk of his fingers he pulls a knot tight; a thin thread of amber light is drawn out of the air from the left along the cord and tied into the knot. His shoulders are hunched forward, his elbows out, all his attention in his fingers. Details that tell his story: (1) hundreds of knotted cords hang from his belt like a heavy fringe, every knot different; (2) the freshest knots glow faintly amber — stolen strength; (3) one thick black knot hangs apart from the others — the deaf knot; (4) his stone fingertips are capped with bronze, worn smooth from tying; (5) a bronze hook for pulling knots tight hangs from his wrist on a thong. jobs.subject_v1: The enemy: the Keeper, the boss of the Library (Earth). Who it is: the first mechanism of the world — a bronze apparatus taller than the shelves that walks between the rows on four knee-jointed legs; it has been oiled for a thousand years and smells like an old mill. It lets no one near the tablets. It is not a person: here the rules about the belt, the head and the arms do not apply. Right now it has found intruders and is stepping toward them. Character: ancient, implacable and majestic — a cathedral that walks. It does not hate; it guards, and it has never stopped. Framing and pose, the moment of the step: the camera is low and looks up; the apparatus towers and fills the frame, its top near the top edge. Its body is a massive bronze housing like the case of a great tower clock, tall and heavy, crowned with a crest of bronze fins; the front of the housing stands open like two cathedral doors, and inside its chest gears turn; at the center the largest gear, ancient, dark and heavy, glows amber — the first gear of the world. Instead of a face, a single great round amber lens set under a heavy bronze brow at the top of its body glares down toward the left. Two of its four long knee-jointed bronze legs are in the frame at its front: one front leg is raised high, its sharp heavy bronze foot about to come down toward the left like a pile driver; the other front leg is planted, and the stone floor has cracked under it. Its lower legs go out of the frame. Details that tell its story: (1) thousand-year-old oil runs down the bronze in dark streaks and drips, glowing amber, from its joints; (2) the first gear is visibly older than all the others — darker, worn, a few of its teeth chipped; (3) its bronze plates carry fine engraved line ornament, polished by the ages; (4) a haze of fine stone dust, like the dust of an old mill, hangs around its legs; (5) its gears are mid-turn, and a glow is building in its chest toward a full revolution. Place: the tops of tall stone shelves that reach only to its chest, stacked with the tablets it guards; the dark vault above; amber light from below.
jobs.subject: The enemy: the Keeper, the boss of the Library (Earth). Appearance: its body is a massive rounded bronze hull, heavy as a bell and armored with overlapping plates like the shell of a great beetle, slung between its legs. In the front of the hull a wide round opening framed by heavy bronze ribs shows its gears turning inside; at the center the largest gear, ancient, dark and heavy, glows amber — the first gear of the world. From the front of the hull juts a heavy bronze head on a thick jointed neck, like the lantern of a lighthouse; instead of a face it has a single great round amber lens that blazes and throws a beam of amber light down toward the left. Its four legs are long and spiked, bent like the legs of a giant spider crab: each has a high, sharp knee that rises above the hull and comes down to a pointed bronze foot like a spear. Framing and pose, the moment of the step: the camera is low and looks up; the Keeper towers and fills the frame. It rears up toward the left: its two front legs are lifted high, their spear-like feet poised above the heroes to strike down; its hull tilts back; its lens glares. Its hind legs go out of the bottom of the frame. Place: the tops of tall stone shelves reach only to its hull, stacked with the tablets it guards; the dark vault above; amber light from below.
